entries.notes: Latin name used by Julius Caesar and Roman sources for the settlement of the Parisii.
Modern French vernacular exonym of the Latin name Lutetia Parisiorum.
Later Latin name used in the late Roman Empire period, transitional form toward 'Paris'.
The French name Paris, derived from Parisius, in continuous use from the early medieval period to the present.
English name for the city, identical to the French form.

events.description: Julius Caesar conquered the Paris Basin and established the Roman settlement of Lutetia on the Left Bank.
Vikings sacked Paris despite the fortification of the Île de la Cité.
Siege of Paris (885–886); successfully defended under Odo of France, Count of Paris.
Paris occupied by England-friendly Burgundian forces during the Hundred Years' War; Henry V of England entered in 1420, establishing outright English occupation until 1436.
events.perpetrator: Dual monarchy of England and France

events.description: St. Bartholomew's Day massacre (24 August 1572): thousands of French Protestants (Huguenots) were killed in Paris, organised by the Catholic League during the French Wars of Religion.

entries.notes: Parisii tribe inhabited the area from at least the mid-3rd century BC.
Julius Caesar conquered the Paris Basin for Rome in 52 BC.
Transition from Republic to Empire under Augustus.
Frankish domination of Gaul following the fall of the Western Roman Empire; Clovis made Paris his capital in 508.
Carolingian dynasty replaced the Merovingians.
Treaty of Verdun divided the Carolingian Empire; Paris fell within West Francia.
Hugh Capet elected king, founding the Capetian dynasty and the Kingdom of France.
Paris occupied by Burgundian forces 1418, then outright English occupation from 1420 under Henry V; ended 1436.

value.name: Dual monarchy of England and France

entries.notes: English occupation of Paris ended in 1436; France restored.
French Revolution; First Republic declared 1792.
Napoleon Bonaparte seized power as First Consul on 18 Brumaire (9 November 1799).
Napoleon proclaimed Emperor.
Bourbon restoration after Napoleon's abdication.
July Revolution brought Louis-Philippe I to power.
Louis-Philippe overthrown; Second Republic established.
Napoleon III proclaimed Emperor.
Third Republic proclaimed during the Franco-Prussian War.
German occupation of France; Vichy regime. Paris under German military administration.
Liberation of Paris 1944; Provisional Government.

value.name: Provisional Government of the French Republic

entries.notes: Fourth Republic established.
Fifth Republic established under de Gaulle; France continues to the present day.
The Parisii were a Gaulish (Celtic) tribe inhabiting the Paris area from at least the mid-3rd century BC.
Roman conquest introduced Roman urban culture to Lutetia.
Frankish Merovingian culture dominant following the fall of the Western Roman Empire and Clovis's establishment of Paris as his capital.
Gaulish spoken by the Parisii; gradually displaced by Latin after the Roman conquest and eventually dying out by around the 5th–6th century.

Latin introduced as the administrative and cultural language of Lutetia following Roman conquest; remained the written and ecclesiastical language well into the medieval period; spoken vernacular Latin gradually evolved into Old French.
Frankish immigration and the mixing of Gaulish Romance with Frankish gave rise to the Francien/Old French dialects in Paris from the Merovingian period onward.
Middle and then Modern French developed from Old French; French has been the primary language of Paris and the state language of France from the late medieval period to the present.
Gaulish/Celtic religion practiced by the Parisii before and during the early Roman period; gradually displaced by Roman religion and then Christianity.
Roman religion became dominant following the conquest of 52 BC; remained state religion until the Christianisation of the Empire.
Christianity introduced mid-3rd century AD by Saint Denis, first Bishop of Paris. Minority religion until official recognition.

Christianity became the state religion of the Roman Empire under Theodosius I (380 AD). The Catholic Church has remained the dominant institution in Paris ever since, though secularisation reduced its state role after the Revolution.
A significant Jewish community existed in medieval Paris. Jews were repeatedly expelled and readmitted; finally expelled from France in 1394.

Protestant (Huguenot) community grew during the Reformation. Paris was a stronghold of the Catholic League; the St. Bartholomew's Day massacre of 1572 targeted Protestants. Edict of Nantes 1598 granted some tolerance.
Jews were emancipated by the French Revolution in 1791, returning as a recognized community in Paris.
Parisii settlement on the Île de la Cité, mid-3rd century BC.
Roman conquest 52 BC; Lutetia Parisiorum established as a Roman town with forum, baths, temples, theatres, and amphitheatre.
Clovis I made Paris the capital of the Frankish kingdom in 508.
Hugh Capet elected king; Paris becomes firmly established as capital of France and grows into the largest and most prosperous city in France.
The article states London had 80,000 inhabitants by 1300, used for comparison; Paris was already larger at this date.
